sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球供应链制造母港、跨境电商货源地与外资合规准入市场

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Tailoring of Licensed Theatrical Costume Robes and Synthetic Wigs

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (codified German-Japanese influenced system; separate commercial registry and regulatory autonomy from the PRC within the cross-strait constitutional asymmetry)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Economic Cooperation Framework Agreement (ECFA) between the Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits (ARATS) and the Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF), signed 2010-06-29
Cross-Strait Investment Protection and Promotion Agreement between ARATS and SEF, signed 2012-08-09
Cross-Strait Agreement on Trade in Services between ARATS and SEF, signed 2013-06-21 (signed but implementation suspended)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act, principally Articles 18, 128-156, 170, 192, 202, 208 and 219-235; Foreign Investment Act and Regulations Governing Investment by Foreign Nationals. Taiwan does not use the PRC statutory WFOE form; the proposed vehicle should be established as a foreign-invested company limited by shares or, if appropriate, a limited company.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Local municipal or county government Department of Economic Development or Economic Affairs responsible for the registered office, with foreign-investment approval handled by the Investment Promotion Administration, Ministry of Economic Affairs.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Company Registration for a Company Limited by Shares, together with the Articles of Incorporation, promoter or shareholder information, foreign-investment approval, capital verification documents and registered-office evidence.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No general statutory minimum paid-up capital applies. The capital must be commercially sufficient for the approved business and paid into the company bank account after foreign-investment approval. A Taiwan certified public accountant must verify the capital contribution; no general statutory escrow account is required, although the bank account and remittance trail must be documented.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company accept and allot the shares subscribed by its foreign shareholder in accordance with the approved investment amount and the Articles of Incorporation, subject to receipt and certification of the paid-in capital. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office at the approved Taiwan address is adopted with effect from incorporation. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name] is appointed Chairperson, [Name] General Manager, and [Name] Company Secretary or authorized filing representative, each to serve subject to the Articles, the Company Act, and applicable foreign-investment approvals. The officers are authorized to complete registration, banking, tax, employment, factory, and regulatory filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm Foreign-Investment Eligibility and Business Activities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Promotion Administration, Ministry of Economic Affairs, and the relevant local government company-registration authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify that apparel, costume, synthetic-wig and prop manufacturing activities are permitted for foreign investment and correctly classified under the Taiwan business-item codes. Prepare the proposed Chinese and English company names, registered address, ownership chart and investment amount. Confirm that any restricted business item is excluded or separately approved.
required_dossiers: Foreign shareholder certificate of incorporation or equivalent
Foreign shareholder constitutional documents and ownership chart
Board or shareholder authorization for Taiwan investment
Passport or identification of responsible person and directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to classification or eligibility queries with revised business items, ownership documents or investment explanations. If a business item is restricted, remove it, obtain sector approval, or submit a separate approval application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve Company Name and Business Scope
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company Name and Business Scope Pre-check service of the local government or the Ministry of Economic Affairs online company-registration platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed Chinese company name, English name where applicable, principal business items and intended company form. Do not execute public-facing contracts under the proposed name until the name is approved. Ensure manufacturing, apparel, costume, wig, prop and online-retail activities are separately and accurately listed.
required_dossiers: Identification of applicant or authorized agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Replace conflicting names or revise business-item wording and resubmit. A rejected business item should be removed or supported by the applicable sector authority's approval.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Promotion Administration, Ministry of Economic Affairs
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the foreign-investment application before capital remittance. Provide the investment amount, source of funds, ownership chain, business plan, proposed capitalization and intended operations. Foreign corporate documents must generally be notarized or legalized in the place of issuance and authenticated or otherwise accepted under Taiwan document rules, with Chinese translations where required.
required_dossiers: Foreign shareholder articles and ownership chart
Board or shareholder resolution approving investment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cure deficiencies within the stated response period by submitting legalized documents, revised investment data, source-of-funds evidence or an amended business plan. Failure to respond may result in closure or rejection of the application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Remit Capital and Obtain CPA Capital Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Designated Taiwan bank and Taiwan certified public accountant
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open the preparatory or company bank account, remit the approved foreign investment through regulated banking channels, retain the inward-remittance certificate and bank statements, and obtain a CPA capital verification report. Do not use undocumented cash, netting or shareholder loans as a substitute for approved equity capital unless separately permitted and documented.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct remittance discrepancies through the bank, obtain a revised remittance certificate, or apply for an approved amendment if the amount or investor differs from the approval.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Statutory Incorporation and Corporate Appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipal or county government Department of Economic Development or Economic Affairs
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt the Articles of Incorporation, appoint directors, supervisors where applicable, Chairperson and General Manager, and execute the first board resolution. File the company-registration application electronically or in paper form with the certified capital documents and registered-office evidence. Use notarization or legalization for foreign documents where required by the registry or foreign-investment authority.
required_dossiers: Minutes of promoter or shareholder meeting
Power of attorney for filing agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Answer the registry's written query, replace defective forms, correct business-item descriptions, and resubmit within the prescribed cure period. If rejected, request the legal basis and file an administrative appeal or a corrected application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Tax, Invoicing and Beneficial-Ownership Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau branch having jurisdiction over the registered office and Ministry of Finance electronic invoice system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company tax account, business tax status, accounting books, electronic invoice profile and withholding-tax obligations. Establish beneficial-owner, related-party and transaction records. Register payroll and withholding systems before making taxable salary, service or dividend payments.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct the tax registration, business address, invoice settings or responsible-person information and resubmit to the competent tax office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local government industrial development or economic affairs department under the Factory Management Act; Industrial Development Administration, Ministry of Economic Affairs, where central review applies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Determine whether the premises and equipment meet the statutory definition and thresholds of a factory. If applicable, secure land-use, building-use and factory-registration approval before commencing production. Verify zoning, power capacity, machinery layout, worker numbers, production processes and fire-safety conditions. A separate sector manufacturing license is generally not required for ordinary apparel or cosplay-prop production, but factory registration may be mandatory.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to inspection findings, correct layout, zoning, safety or equipment deficiencies, and request reinspection. Do not commence regulated factory operations until the registration or applicable exemption is documented.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Environmental, Fire and Occupational Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Environment and local environmental protection bureau; local fire department; Occupational Safety and Health Administration or competent local labor authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Screen the project under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act and obtain any required air, wastewater, waste, noise or hazardous-material permits before operation. Obtain fire-safety inspection approval for the premises and maintain compliant exits, extinguishers, electrical systems and storage. Implement occupational risk assessments, machine guarding, chemical controls, training, incident reporting and worker health protections under the Occupational Safety and Health Act.
required_dossiers: Air-emission and wastewater applications, if applicable
Chemical inventory and safety data sheets
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cure inspection deficiencies, submit missing monitoring data, obtain amended permits, and request reinspection. Environmental violations may result in administrative penalties, remediation orders, suspension or criminal referral.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Industrial Development Administration, Ministry of Economic Affairs, together with the relevant municipal or county government industrial development or economic affairs department. Ordinary cosplay apparel and prop manufacturing generally has no separate product-sector manufacturing license, but statutory factory registration may apply to qualifying premises and equipment.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Factory Registration Certificate under the Factory Management Act, if the premises satisfy the statutory factory criteria; otherwise, the applicable local business registration and premises-use approvals.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment, Taiwan, and the competent local Environmental Protection Bureau
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Normally Registration or Exempt after project screening for small-scale apparel and prop manufacturing; Full EIA Report may be required if statutory location, land-use, scale, emissions, wastewater, hazardous-material or development thresholds are triggered.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with the Water Pollution Control Act and applicable sector discharge standards; obtain a wastewater permit where discharge is regulated. Comply with the Air Pollution Control Act for particulate matter, VOCs and process emissions, with permit-specific limits based on equipment and emission calculations. Segregate, label, store and transfer general, industrial and hazardous waste under the Waste Disposal Act using licensed contractors and manifests. No single universal VOC or wastewater threshold applies without the confirmed site, process, equipment and discharge route.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain local fire-department inspection approval and maintain approved evacuation routes, emergency lighting, alarms, extinguishers, electrical protection and fire-compartmentation. Confirm building-use approval, structural load capacity and machinery anchoring for production, storage and mezzanine areas. Comply with the Occupational Safety and Health Act, including machine guarding, electrical safety, chemical labeling, ventilation, personal protective equipment, worker training, emergency response and statutory accident reporting.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China; official national portal at https://www.chinatax.gov.cn; electronic filing and digital invoice services through the Electronic Tax Bureau (etax.chinatax.gov.cn); national taxpayer service hotline 12366; export/customs data exchange through the China International Trade Single Window (singlewindow.cn). A WFOE registers with the local competent tax authority at its place of business in mainland China.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) is established under the Foreign Investment Law and the PRC Company Law by registration with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR). Upon issuance of the business license, the WFOE automatically receives an 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), which constitutes its statutory taxpayer identification number (TIN) and VAT registration identifier. SAMR transmits the registration to the STA in real time under the one-certificate-one-code reform. The WFOE must then complete, within 30 days of the license date: (1) verification of the auto-populated tax registration profile (VAT, corporate income tax, stamp duty, urban construction tax, education surcharges, and social insurance) in the Electronic Tax Bureau; (2) status determination as a general VAT taxpayer where annual taxable sales will exceed RMB 5 million; (3) export tax rebate (exemption) registration with the competent tax authority, including risk-grade assessment; (4) China Customs exporter registration through the Single Window, using the same USCC; (5) opening of a basic deposit account and a foreign-exchange settlement account with a designated bank, execution of the tripartite tax-bank-enterprise direct withholding agreement, and appointment of a financial officer; and (6) enrolment, where applicable, for cross-border e-commerce customs supervision codes 9610 (B2C) and 9710 (B2B) for sales made through Stripe or Shopify Payments to Taiwan or other markets. Taiwan-resident investors may hold 100% of WFOE equity under cross-strait investment rules; no minimum registered capital is required, and capital contribution records remain relevant for the financial accounting profile behind the TIN.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: China does not operate a check-the-box entity-classification election. A PRC WFOE is mandatorily a resident enterprise for corporate income tax (CIT), taxed at entity level on worldwide income. Available statutory elections relevant to an exporting manufacturer include: (1) the VAT status election between small-scale taxpayer and general VAT taxpayer, with mandatory general status above RMB 5,000,000 annual taxable sales and voluntary registration below that threshold; (2) the VAT simplified levy method for selected out-of-scope transactions (e.g., a 3% deemed levy rate, with the temporary 1% levy for small-scale taxpayers in force to 31 December 2027); (3) the export tax rebate method election, under which production-export enterprises apply the exemption-credit-refund model and trading-export enterprises apply the exemption-refund model, with a restricted one-off election for mixed manufacturing-trading operations subject to separate accounting; (4) the small low-profit enterprise (SLPE) CIT election, effective when taxable income does not exceed RMB 3,000,000, employees do not exceed 300, and total assets do not exceed RMB 5,000,000, yielding a 5% effective CIT rate; (5) the election to claim a 100% additional CIT deduction for eligible R&D expenditure on fabric technology and costume manufacturing innovation; and (6) hybrid mismatch treatment, under which the Special Tax Adjustment Measures and Article 47 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law allow the STA to re-characterize or disallow deductions for cross-border payments excluded from the recipient's taxable income, thereby neutralizing hybrid financial instrument outcomes; no unilateral entity-classification election is available in China.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: RMB 5,000,000 in annual taxable sales of goods or services triggers mandatory general VAT taxpayer registration; businesses below this threshold are registered small-scale taxpayers charged at a 3% levy rate (temporarily reduced to 1% through 31 December 2027), with a monthly sales exemption of RMB 100,000 for small-scale taxpayers through 31 December 2027. VAT registration itself arises automatically upon issuance of the business license; the RMB 5,000,000 rolling 12-month turnover is the operative threshold for status change to a general VAT taxpayer.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China requires the use of the Fully Digitalized Electronic Invoice (FDEI) under the Golden Tax Phase IV administration. All VAT invoices for B2B and B2C transactions must be issued through the national Electronic Tax Bureau platform or a certified third-party e-invoice service provider connected by API; each FDEI carries a unique 20-digit invoice number, a QR code, and an electronic verification seal, and the invoice data is transmitted to the STA data warehouse in real time. No paper invoice or physical fiscal stamp is permitted for registered general taxpayers. For exports, the exporter must lodge the customs declaration electronically through the China International Trade Single Window; customs release data, export manifests, payment-platform settlement files, and FX records are automatically matched against the export tax rebate declaration before refund clearance. For cross-border e-commerce retail and B2B flows under supervision codes 9610 and 9710, order-level transaction data, logistics manifests, and Stripe/Shopify settlement reports must be reconciled with the customs release record and the corresponding FDEI, with no exemption from real-time digital clearance.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE, 国家外汇管理局) under the People's Bank of China (PBOC, 中国人民银行); SAFE provincial/municipal branches administer FDI registration, trade-in-goods verification, and capital account settlement for the WFOE's manufacturing site within the Jiangsu/Zhejiang/Guangdong export corridor.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: CNY is fully convertible on current-account items (export proceeds, dividends, service fees) subject to bank authenticity and consistency verification, but capital-account items remain controlled: FDI equity injection requires SAFE FDI registration and is credited to a dedicated capital account with use restrictions (no direct remittance for non-operating purposes such as real estate or equity investment outside the approved business scope). Profit remittance to the Taiwan shareholder is open-account permissible after each fiscal year end, conditioned on a licensed CPA audit, corporate income tax withholding clearance (10% dividend withholding, reduced to 5% where the Cross-Strait Double Taxation Arrangement of 2015 applies for a Taiwan resident company beneficially holding ≥25%), a shareholders' dividend resolution, and the bank's verification against the audited net profit. Capital repatriation by equity transfer or liquidation requires SAFE/AMR approval, state tax clearance, and a post-action reporting filing.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: China abolished mandatory surrender of export receipts in 2012; the WFOE may retain export earnings in a foreign-currency current account or convert to CNY at prevailing market rates at any time. Under the trade-in-goods total-amount verification regime, proceeds from customs-cleared exports must be collected generally within 90 days of the customs declaration date; where collection is expected beyond 90 days (deferred receipt), the WFOE must file a deferred-receipt report with SAFE through the banking system within 30 days of the scheduled maturity, and any such deferred outstanding balances count against the enterprise's trade-credit quota (A-class ceiling of 30% of prior-year export volume). Advance payments received before shipment must be reported within 15 days of receipt and liquidated against customs declarations within the prescribed 180-day turnaround for A-class enterprises. No mandatory conversion ratio applies to the retained hard-currency balances.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (FDI Foreign-Exchange Capital Account) + RMB Basic Deposit Account
Operational Account + Foreign-Currency Current Account (USD/HKD) with online spot settlement
Operational Account + Cross-border e-commerce collection account (licenced PSP sweep and aggregation)
Operational Account + Trade Finance Desk (commercial LC confirmation)
Operational Account + Cross-strait RMB clearing service (CIPS direct participant)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium: offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Wise, Payoneer, Airwallex) cannot establish a SAFE-registered capital account for a mainland WFOE and are not permitted to act as primary settlement banks for FDI or trade-in-goods payments. They may be used only as auxiliary collection conduits for cross-border e-commerce payouts from Shopify/Stripe, strictly routed through a licensed onshore payment institution (PingPong, Lianlian Pay, Alipay Cross-border, or CMB's SwiftGo) that sweeps aggregated settlements into the WFOE's onshore operational account. Any direct offshore EMI custody of the WFOE's export proceeds would breach SAFE repatriation obligations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory physical appearance: the legal representative and the designated financial principal (first authorized signatory) must attend an in-person KYC interview and sign the account-opening documents at the bank's brick-and-mortar branch; remote video acceptance is not permitted for initial corporate account opening. The bank must additionally complete a field visit to the registered manufacturing address (factory floor, equipment, inventory) before activating the FDI capital account; directors resident in Taiwan may delegate by notarized power of attorney but the mainland-appointed legal representative must appear personally.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Taiwan (TW) beneficial ownership and cross-strait capital sensitization
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized Certificate of Incorporation and Articles of Incorporation of the Taiwan shareholder; trust/company registry chart and beneficial ownership declaration; board resolution approving the FDI injection schedule; a business narrative demonstrating substantive manufacturing in China (factory lease, sewing and wig production line equipment purchase invoices, payroll records for ≥20 local staff); commitment letter against round-tripping of Chinese-origin funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: IP royalty ambiguity around licensed cosplay character designs
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: IP license agreements with Western/Japanese licensors; royalty computation memos; contractual segregation of physical-goods licensing fees from intangible service fees; confirmation that all inbound receipts correspond to goods exports with matching customs declarations rather than off-balance-sheet software/royalty inflows requiring separate tax filing and fee deductions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency, low-amount e-commerce payouts (Stripe/Shopify Payments) creating velocity mismatch vs. shipment documentation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Platform settlement reports (Gross receipts, payouts, refunds) mapped SKU-wise to customs single-window export declarations; third-party logistics (3PL) bills of lading and delivery confirmations; a documented treasury policy separating direct-to-consumer payout receipts from commercial LC and B2B wire receipts, with monthly reconciliation submitted to the relationship manager.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Dormancy or inactive-account risk before capital escalation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital utilization plan (tooling/molds/cutting machines, wig material procurement, warehouse fit-out); signed purchase orders from licensors or retail chains; quarterly CPA capital verification reports (验资报告) evidencing the paid-in schedule under the Company Law 2024 five-year contribution deadline; proactive monthly transaction activity via employee payroll and utility payments to avoid frozen-account triggers.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The Taiwan parent remits USD or HKD through SWIFT MT103 to the WFOE's FDI Foreign-Exchange Capital Account at ICBC/BOC, referencing the SAFE FDI Registration Certificate (FDI业务登记凭证) and transaction purpose code 622 (foreign direct investment capital injection). The receiving bank must match the remittance against the SAFE system, settle the foreign currency into CNY under the capital settlement mechanism at the prevailing central parity-based spot rate, and credit the RMB expenditure account, strictly monitoring designated-use compliance (capex, raw materials, payroll, and ordinary overhead; prohibited for securities, wealth-management products, or real estate outside the registered business scope unless approved). All injection tranches must be completed within the five-year statutory contribution period and reported via the monthly SAFE cross-border flow monitoring file.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For payments to third-party suppliers (fabric, wig fiber, zippers, packaging, freight forwarders): SWIFT MT103 for amounts up to USD 500,000; Commercial Letters of Credit (sight or usance 90–180 days) issued through BOC/ICBC trade desks for amounts above USD 500,000, ensuring two-party authenticity verification against contracts and customs declarations. Domestic RMB supplier payments are cleared via CIPS (Cross-Border Interbank Payment System) direct/indirect participant banks. Export collections: B2B buyers wire to the WFOE's BOC foreign-currency account; DTC e-commerce receipts from Shopify Payments/Stripe are aggregated and settled through a licensed PSP (PingPong/Lianlian/CMB SwiftGo) and swept onshore daily into the CMB RMB account, with each sweep referenced to the corresponding customs declaration for SAFE trade-in-goods verification.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CNY/USD Forward Contracts (real trade background, maturity up to 12 months, required SAFE forward-settlement verification)
CNY/USD Foreign-Exchange Swaps (onshore, via licensed bank proprietary desk)
Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swaps (CCIRS) aligning USD-denominated export receipts with CNY operating costs
CNY/USD Plain-Vanilla European Call/Put Options and Zero-Cost Collars (trade-hedge purpose only)
FX Forward Settlement between CNY and HKD/JPY (the latter relevant for cosplay raw-material imports from Japanese fabric suppliers)
Onshore combinations of the above under the 'Real Need-Based Hedging' principle; offshore CNY NDFs are prohibited for onshore WFOEs

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Shareholders' Meeting – adoption of financial statements, operating reports, and profit-distribution proposals
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate governance – documented in minutes; no external filing (recorded with company secretary)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 6 months after fiscal year-end (calendar-year companies: by 30 June)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Competent authority may impose NT$10,000–50,000 fine and order rectification; continued failure may lead to court-appointed convener

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual final-beneficiary/UBO declaration under Company Act Article 22-1 (directors, supervisors, managers, and shareholders holding >10% capital or shares)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Taiwan Depository & Clearing Corporation (TDCC) platform designated by the Ministry of Economic Affairs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 – 31 March annually; any shareholding transfer affecting >10% holder status must be reported within 15 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or false filing: NT$50,000–5,000,000 fine per violation, with repeated escalation if uncorrected

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual withholding-tax statement (salary, dividend, royalties, and other withheld income) for the preceding year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau (Ministry of Finance), territorial tax administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 – 31 January of the following year (extended to the next business day if deadline falls on holiday)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-filing: penalty of NT$7,500–45,000 per form, plus surcharges on un-withheld amounts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax return and undistributed-surplus (retained earnings) taxation statement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau (Ministry of Finance), local branch of the competent tax office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 – 31 May of the following year (calendar-year companies; optional extension to 30 June without penalty for properly submitted provisional returns)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing: 10% surcharge (up to NT$30,000) if filed within 30 days after deadline; 20% negligence amount surcharge (up to NT$90,000) after 30 days; underpayment triggers tax adjustment and fines of up to 2–3× the understated tax

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit (certified public accountant review) is required when annual paid-in capital reaches NT$30,000,000 (≈USD 970,000) or annual net revenue reaches NT$100,000,000 (≈USD 3,200,000); mandatory for all publicly-issued companies; otherwise financial statements may be prepared internally and must be approved by shareholders
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Taiwan IFRS (for publicly-traded/issued companies) or Taiwan Business Accounting Standards under the Business Accounting Act for non-public privately-held limited companies; books must be maintained in New Taiwan Dollars in Chinese language

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annually between 1–31 March, every non-public company must submit to the TDCC online platform a complete list of directors, supervisors, managers, and shareholders holding >10% of issued shares or paid-in capital; any shareholding transfer resulting in a covered-person change must be separately reported within 15 calendar days; failure constitutes a Company Act Article 22-1 violation

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $400 – $1,200 per year for registered office address; $800 – $2,000 per year for full corporate secretarial retainer
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $1,500 – $5,000 per year for a standard private service entity with limited transactions

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Flat 20% on profit-seeking enterprise taxable income; 5% retained-earnings surtax on undistributed earnings under Article 66-9; first NT$120,000 of taxable income is exempt; participation exemption for domestic dividends; R&D investment tax credit up to 15% of qualifying research expenditures (capped at 30% of tax payable); foreign tax credit available for taxes paid by the Taiwan WFOE on foreign-source branch income; basic (minimum) tax rate 12% applicable only to enterprises enjoying large preferential exemptions under the AMT statute.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return (營利事業所得稅結算申報書) filed electronically via the Taiwan Ministry of Finance e-Tax E-Filing Network (電子申報繳稅服務網, tax.nat.gov.tw)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing period from 1 May to 31 May following the fiscal year-end; automatic extension to 30 June where the enterprise's financial statements are audited and certified by a CPA

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification number (統一編號), company name, address, fiscal year-end, business registration code, industry code (ISIC 3240 / local Taiwan industry code), and the responsible person's ID.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Taiwan WFOE's own tax ID and local detail. The non-resident parent is not named in this return; parent details are recorded in the company registry and in withholding forms at distribution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting principles adopted, bookkeeping basis, and currency. Taiwan IFRS / local GAAP with New Taiwan Dollar functional currency is mandatory.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconciliation to foreign parent GAAP is not accepted; the foreign parent's accounting policies do not govern the Taiwan statutory books.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 10 (Net Sales Revenue 營業收入)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total net operating revenue from fabrication and tailoring of cosplay costumes, theatrical robes, synthetic wigs, props, and accessories, including online sales settled through Shopify/Stripe and other cross-border payment rails.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all Taiwan-source and effectively-connected revenue. Sales directly executed by the foreign parent without a Taiwan PE are not reportable here; if the WFOE merely assists the parent, only commission/service income is reportable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 20 (Cost of Goods Sold 營業成本)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct materials (fabrics, fibers, dyes), licensed-character input costs, direct labor, factory overhead, and freight-in attributable to the cosplay apparel manufacturing operations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Related-party purchases must be priced at arm's length and substantiated by a Transfer Pricing Local File where thresholds are met; no arbitrary uplift of intercompany purchase prices is permitted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 30 (Gross Operating Income 營業毛利)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net sales revenue minus cost of goods sold.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the WFOE carries no inventory risk and acts as a buy-sell agent for the parent, this line should show only the distribution margin, not full gross margin.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 40 (Operating Expenses 營業費用及損失)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selling, general and administrative expenses: salaries, factory rents, utilities, depreciation, platform transaction fees (Stripe/Shopify fees), customs duties, insurance, and professional service fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Service fees paid to the non-resident parent or affiliated parties are deductible only if genuine, arm's-length, and substantiated; the payer must withhold and remit 20% gross-basis WHT on taxable Taiwanese-source service fees of non-residents.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit derived solely from the Taiwan manufacturing and sales activity of the WFOE.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocation of head-office expenses is not permitted for a domestically incorporated subsidiary; the WFOE is a separate taxable entity and cannot claim the parent's home-office costs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest income, foreign-exchange gains, rental income, licensing royalties received, and other non-operating income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Royalties received by the Taiwan entity from foreign licensees are taxable as Taiwan-source profit-seeking income if the exploitation/bearing of right is attributable to the Taiwan business; foreign tax credits may apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest expense, foreign-exchange losses, casualty losses, and other non-operating deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid to a non-resident related lender is deductible only at arm's-length rates and subject to 15% gross-basis WHT; excessive interest from tax-haven affiliates may be disallowed pursuant to interest-stripping rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 80 (Net Income Before Tax 全年所得額)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total profit after all operating and non-operating items, before applying loss carryforwards and tax exemptions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is the starting point for the statutory 20% headline rate; no parent-consolidated group relief is available.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 90 (Taxable Income After Loss Carryforwards 課稅所得額)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income reduced by tax-exempt income and prior-year qualifying operating-loss deductions (10-year carryforward under Article 39).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses are available to the WFOE only, not to the foreign shareholder; losses of a foreign head office cannot be used.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 100 (Income Tax Payable 應納稅額)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income multiplied by 20%, reduced by R&D tax credits, foreign tax credits, AMT differential, and provisional tax installments previously paid.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Shareholder-level dividend withholding of 21% on distributions to non-residents is computed on a separate Withholding Tax Return (Form 10/17), not in this annual return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule M (Minimum/AMT Reconciliation 所得基本稅額)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of alternative minimum tax where preferential exemptions cause the effective rate to fall below 12%; basic income exceeds NT$6.5 million and AMT liability is compared with regular tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A typical manufacturing/retail WFOE with no tax-holiday preference is ordinarily not subject to AMT; any foreign tax exemption claims must still be scheduled.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: surcharge of 10% of assessed tax for each two-month period or fraction thereof of delay, up to a maximum of 30% of assessed tax; where no tax is due, a fine of NT$3,000 to NT$30,000. Underreporting or false return: fine from two times to three times the underpaid tax, plus overdue interest. Willful evasion triggers criminal prosecution under the Tax Collection Act Article 41 (imprisonment up to five years, detention, and/or fines).
